title: ChatGPT Health adds Epic integration for clinicians to import patient data
slides: Can ChatGPT Health truly streamline your clinical workflow?
Epic integration now imports patient data directly.
It bypasses the clipboard—but not the liability.
You'll save minutes per note, yet face new risks.
Test it on one patient before trusting automation.
thread_text:
1. ChatGPT Health: Too Good to Be True?

Epic's new integration lets the AI pull patient data directly, but the liability for errors still sits with you.

2. The Clipboard Is Just a Workaround

It bypasses the manual copy-paste, yet every word the AI writes becomes your responsibility—a risky trade-off for convenience.

3. Save Minutes, Risk More

You'll cut note time down significantly, but new errors may slip past your review—errors that could harm patients or lead to lawsuits.

4. The Liability You Can't Ignore

Unlike a clipboard, AI errors are unpredictable. You can't just blame the tool—you own the outcome, legally and ethically.

5. Test Before You Trust

Run one patient with low risk through the AI workflow. See where it fails. If you haven't done this yet, start there.

instagram.caption:
Your next patient note could write itself—but if it’s wrong, it’s on you. 🩺

ChatGPT Health now pulls data straight from Epic, skipping the copy-paste. Clinicians save minutes per note, but every AI-generated word becomes their legal responsibility. Errors are unpredictable, not like a clipboard mistake you can spot.

For anyone documenting care: your workflow just got faster, but your liability just got bigger. ⚖️

Test it on one low-risk patient first. Where did it fail? If you haven't run that trial yet, that's your next move. ✍️
